paper_title: Tirzepatide for Weight Reduction in Chinese Adults With Obesity: The SURMOUNT-CN Randomized Clinical Trial.
design_rationale: The study explicitly states that participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to tirzepatide 10 mg, tirzepatide 15 mg, or placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment and balanced group sizes are reported, but the supplied text does not describe sequence generation, allocation concealment, or baseline comparability by treatment group.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to receive once-weekly, subcutaneous 10-mg (n = 70) or 15-mg (n = 71) tirzepatide or placebo (n = 69).

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind, all groups received the same background lifestyle intervention, and efficacy analyses used the intention-to-treat population, reducing concern about intervention-related deviations and inappropriate analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 clinical trial... Efficacy and safety analyses were performed on an intention-to-treat population.

domain_judgments.rationale: Trial completion was very high at 95.7%, and fewer than 5% discontinued treatment because of adverse events, making material bias from missing outcome data unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of 210 randomized participants... 201 (95.7%) completed the trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: Body weight and prespecified weight-loss thresholds are objective and were measured at the same time point across groups in a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, so differential measurement is unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Co–primary end points were the percent change in body weight from baseline and weight reduction of at least 5% at week 52.

domain_judgments.rationale: The co-primary outcomes and trial registration are reported, but the supplied text provides no protocol or statistical analysis plan against which to verify that outcome measurements and analyses were selected as prespecified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Co–primary end points were the percent change in body weight from baseline and weight reduction of at least 5% at week 52.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns, driven by insufficient detail in the supplied text about sequence generation and allocation concealment and the inability to verify reported analyses against a protocol or statistical analysis plan. Blinding, intention-to-treat analysis, high completion, and objective weight outcomes otherwise support low risk.

paper_title: Tirzepatide once weekly for the treatment of obesity in people with type 2 diabetes (SURMOUNT-2): a double-blind, randomised, multicentre, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
design_rationale: Participants were explicitly assigned 1:1:1 using a computer-generated random sequence implemented through a validated interactive web-response system.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated and implemented through a validated web-response system, treatment assignment was masked, and reported baseline characteristics were generally balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Assignment to treatment group was determined by a computer-generated random sequence using a validated interactive web-response system.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, investigators, and sponsor were masked; placebo matched active treatment; co-interventions were protocolized; and efficacy endpoints used all randomized participants under an estimand that included discontinuation and rescue therapy.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All participants, investigators, and the sponsor were masked to treatment assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Study completion was high at 92%, but attrition was differential (95%, 91%, and 89% across groups), and week-72 missing outcomes were imputed, leaving some potential for bias if missingness depended on unobserved outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Overall, 92% [859] of participants completed the study (95% [296], 91% [282], and 89% [281] with tirzepatide 10 mg, tirzepatide 15 mg, and placebo, respectively).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was an objective body-weight measurement assessed according to the same protocol across groups, and masking of participants and investigators reduced the likelihood that knowledge of assignment influenced measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All participants, investigators, and the sponsor were masked to treatment assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, endpoints and estimands were prespecified, and multiplicity was controlled using a prespecified graphical testing procedure, providing little indication of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The type 1 error rate was controlled at a level of 0·05 within each estimand for evaluation of primary and key secondary objectives via a graphical testing approach.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns, driven by modest and differential missing outcome data handled through imputation. Randomization, masking, objective outcome measurement, intention-to-treat estimands, prospective registration, and prespecified multiplicity control otherwise support low risk.

paper_title: Tirzepatide after intensive lifestyle intervention in adults with overweight or obesity: the SURMOUNT-3 phase 3 trial.
design_rationale: This was a parallel-group randomized controlled trial; eligible lead-in responders were assigned 1:1 using a computer-generated random sequence implemented through a validated interactive web-response system.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was explicitly computer-generated, implemented through a validated centralized web-response system, stratified on prespecified factors, and baseline characteristics were reported as similar across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Assignment to treatment group was determined by a computer-generated random sequence using a validated interactive web-response system.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, investigators, and the sponsor were masked with identical pens, co-interventions were applied similarly, and the primary treatment-regimen estimand included all randomized participants regardless of adherence with appropriate handling of discontinuation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All participants, investigators and the sponsor were masked to treatment assignment. To maintain masking of participants and site staff, the single-dose pens were identical between active product and placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: Study and on-treatment completion were incomplete and differed by group, particularly for placebo, and although prespecified hybrid imputation used retrieved dropouts and available data, bias from outcome-dependent missingness cannot be fully excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 579 randomized participants, 479 (82.7%) completed the study (87.8% on tirzepatide MTD and 77.7% on placebo) and 429 (74.1%) completed the study on treatment (78.7% on tirzepatide MTD and 69.5% on placebo).

domain_judgments.rationale: Body weight is an objective and appropriate outcome measured consistently across randomized groups, and masking of participants and investigators further limits differential measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This 84-week, multicenter, randomized, parallel-arm, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial was conducted at 62 medical research centers in the USA, Argentina and Brazil.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, the protocol and statistical analysis plan were available, coprimary and key secondary endpoints and two estimands were prespecified, and multiplicity was controlled for confirmatory outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Primary and key secondary endpoints were controlled for type 1 error at a two-sided significance level of 0.05 within each estimand via a graphical testing approach.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns, driven by substantial and differential study/treatment discontinuation and reliance on imputation assumptions for missing week-72 outcomes. Randomization, masking, objective outcome measurement, and prespecified reporting were otherwise robust.

paper_title: Tirzepatide for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Obesity
design_rationale: The two phase 3 trials explicitly used 1:1 random assignment to tirzepatide or placebo through a Web-based interactive response system.

domain_judgments.rationale: A centralized Web-based system generated and implemented stratified 1:1 randomization, masking was maintained, and reported baseline differences were compatible with chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was conducted by means of a Web-based interactive response system and stratified according to trial, country or geographic region, baseline AHI severity category, and sex.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, investigators, and the sponsor were blinded and the treatment-regimen estimand included participants irrespective of treatment discontinuation, but adherence differed substantially by arm and treatment-related gastrointestinal effects could have revealed assignment, creating some potential for differential behavioral deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Overall, 82.9% of the participants completed the trial (91.5% in the tirzepatide groups and 74.4% in the placebo groups) and 79.7% adhered to the assigned regimen (87.6% in the tirzepatide groups and 71.9% in the placebo groups).

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 82.9% completed the trials, with marked differential completion between tirzepatide and placebo, and although prespecified multiple imputation addressed missing-at-random and not-at-random scenarios, bias from substantial differential missingness cannot be excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Overall, 82.9% of the participants completed the trial (91.5% in the tirzepatide groups and 74.4% in the placebo groups).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary AHI outcome was objectively measured at the same scheduled times using laboratory polysomnography and centrally scored under a standardized rule, while trial-group masking reduced assessor-influence concerns.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The AHI was measured by laboratory polysomnography at screening, week 20, and week 52. Data from polysomnographic studies were scored centrally with the use of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine rule 1B.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered, the protocol and statistical analysis plan were available, the primary endpoint was prespecified, multiplicity was controlled, and the analysis plan was finalized before database lock and unblinding; the disclosed secondary-PRO change was also made before unblinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The statistical analysis plan, including all the end points and assessments, was finalized and submitted before the time of the database lock and data unblinding.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns, driven by substantial and differential trial completion and regimen adherence, despite prespecified treatment-regimen analyses and multiple imputation. Randomization, objective centralized outcome measurement, and prespecified reporting were otherwise robust.

design_rationale: The trial explicitly states that 731 eligible patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to tirzepatide or matching placebo, with stratification by recent heart-failure decompensation, type 2 diabetes, and BMI.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment, stratification, double blinding, and balanced baseline characteristics are reported, but the method used to generate the sequence and the mechanism ensuring allocation concealment are not described in the supplied text.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eligible patients were randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio and in a double-blind manner, to receive tirzepatide subcutaneously at a dose of 2.5 mg per week or placebo

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial used matching placebo and double blinding, followed all randomized patients regardless of treatment continuation, and analyzed both primary endpoints according to intention to treat; although discontinuation differed somewhat, this was handled by the treatment-policy analysis and there is no evidence of outcome-affecting deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In accordance with the intention-to-treat principle, for both primary end points, the analysis was based on all patients who underwent randomization and included the entire planned treatment period, regardless of whether patients continued receiving tirzepatide or placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: Final-visit attendance exceeded 90% in both groups, vital-status loss was small, all randomized patients were followed for major outcomes where possible, and missing 52-week KCCQ-CSS data were addressed with prespecified multiple imputation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 332 patients (91.2%) in the tirzepatide group and 331 patients (90.2%) in the placebo group attended the final trial visit.

domain_judgments.rationale: Cardiovascular deaths and worsening heart-failure events were assessed using prespecified definitions by a blinded adjudication committee, while KCCQ-CSS was measured identically across groups in a double-blind placebo-controlled design.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A clinical events committee adjudicated events in a blinded manner according to prespecified definitions.

domain_judgments.rationale: A protocol and statistical analysis plan were available and the revised primary endpoints and multiplicity control were prespecified before unblinding, but the primary endpoints were materially changed during the trial in light of external findings, leaving some concern about outcome selection despite the reported safeguards.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Accordingly, on the basis of reasons external to the trial, the primary end points were revised approximately 1 year before the end of the trial, with the investigators and the sponsor having no knowledge of the unblinded data and before the data and safety monitoring committee had conducted any efficacy analyses.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged some concerns, driven by absent details on sequence generation and allocation concealment and by the mid-trial revision of the primary endpoints. Blinding, intention-to-treat analyses, outcome adjudication, and largely complete follow-up otherwise support low risk in the remaining domains.

paper_title: Efficacy and safety of once-weekly tirzepatide in Japanese patients with obesity disease (SURMOUNT-J): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial
design_rationale: Participants were explicitly assigned 1:1:1 using a computer-generated random sequence implemented through a central interactive web response system.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated and centrally implemented, treatment assignment was concealed through the interactive web response system and masking, and reported baseline characteristics were well balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Treatment assignment was determined by a computer-generated random sequence using a central interactive web response system. Investigators, site staf, participants, and sponsor were blinded to treatment assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding and common lifestyle counselling limited differential deviations, but the primary efficacy estimand excluded post-discontinuation data and treatment discontinuation differed somewhat across groups, although a treatment-regimen sensitivity analysis supported the findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The eficacy analysis set was used, which included data obtained during the treatment period, excluding data after discontinuation of study drug. Supplementary eficacy analyses were conducted using the treatment regimen estimand.

domain_judgments.rationale: Study retention was high and sensitivity analyses were consistent, but only 85% completed both treatment and study, discontinuation varied by group, and the primary analysis relied on model-based imputation under assumptions that could be affected by treatment-related dropout.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of 225 participants, 192 (85%) completed both study and treatment whereas 215 (96%) completed the study regardless of whether they completed treatment... Missing bodyweight measurements at week 72 were imputed using predicted values from MMRM.

domain_judgments.rationale: The coprimary outcomes were objective bodyweight measurements assessed under double blinding, with the same procedures across randomized groups, making differential measurement error unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Investigators, site staf, participants, and sponsor were blinded to treatment assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, its coprimary endpoints and estimands were prespecified, and the report describes multiplicity control and presents both efficacy- and treatment-regimen-estimand results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04844918... The coprimary endpoints were the mean percent change in bodyweight and the proportion of participants achieving at least 5% bodyweight reduction at week 72.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns, driven by the primary efficacy estimand's exclusion of post-treatment-discontinuation data and model-based handling of missing outcomes amid somewhat differential treatment discontinuation. Randomization, blinding, objective outcome measurement, prospective registration, and consistent treatment-regimen sensitivity analyses otherwise support low risk.

paper_title: Continued Treatment With Tirzepatide for Maintenance of Weight Reduction in Adults With Obesity: The SURMOUNT-4 Randomized Clinical Trial.
design_rationale: At week 36, eligible lead-in completers were explicitly assigned 1:1 using a computer-generated random sequence implemented through an interactive web-response system.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated and implemented through an interactive web-response system, with stratification and balanced baseline characteristics supporting a sound randomization process.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: participants who attained the maximum tolerated dose of tirzepatide (10 or 15 mg) were randomized in a 1:1 ratio by a computer-generated random sequence using an interactive web-response system

domain_judgments.rationale: The randomized period was double-blind with matching placebo, all participants received the same lifestyle counseling, and the primary treatment-regimen estimand included all randomized participants regardless of adherence, minimizing bias from deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The treatment regimen estimand was conducted on the full analysis set representing the mean treatment effect of tirzepatide relative to placebo for all participants who had undergone randomization, regardless of treatment adherence.

domain_judgments.rationale: Approximately 10% did not complete the study and discontinuation was more often related to lack of efficacy in the placebo group; although prespecified multiple imputation and estimand methods addressed missingness, outcome-dependent missingness cannot be fully excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the randomized participants, 600 (89.6%) completed the study and 575 (85.8%) completed the study while receiving the study drug. Withdrawal and “other” (mainly in the placebo group as lack of efficacy) were the most common reasons for premature study drug discontinuation during the double-blind period.

domain_judgments.rationale: Body weight is an objective and appropriate primary outcome measured consistently across randomized groups, so knowledge of assignment would be unlikely to materially influence measurement even if blinding were compromised by treatment effects.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary end point was the percent change in body weight from randomization (week 36) to week 88.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, its primary outcome and estimands were prespecified, a statistical analysis plan was available, and multiplicity was controlled for the primary and key secondary outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The type I error rate was controlled within each estimand independently for evaluation of primary and key secondary end points with a graphical approach

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged some concerns, driven by roughly 10% study noncompletion and potentially outcome-related differential discontinuation, despite prespecified imputation and treatment-regimen analyses. Randomization, deviations, objective outcome measurement, and selective reporting were otherwise at low risk.

paper_title: Tirzepatide Once Weekly for the Treatment of Obesity.
design_rationale: The study explicitly reports that 2539 participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to three tirzepatide dose groups or matching placebo in a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although allocation was explicitly randomized, stratified, and produced generally similar baseline groups, the article does not describe the sequence-generation method or allocation concealment sufficiently to establish low risk.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Treatment randomization was stratified by country, sex, and the presence or absence of prediabetes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and trial personnel were blinded with matching placebo, both groups received the same lifestyle intervention, and the primary treatment-regimen estimand used all randomized participants regardless of discontinuation, although adherence was lower in placebo.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Both efficacy and safety end points were analyzed with data from all randomly assigned participants (intention-to-treat population).

domain_judgments.rationale: Completion was 86.0% overall and only 77.0% in placebo, with differential nonadherence and imputation of missing week-72 outcomes, so some dependence of results on unverifiable missing-data assumptions remains despite appropriate modeling.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Overall, 86.0% of participants completed the primary trial treatment period (88.4% to 89.8% across the tirzepatide groups and 77.0% in the placebo group).

domain_judgments.rationale: Body weight is an objective and appropriate outcome measured at the same scheduled time across groups, and the double-blind, matching-placebo design limits influence from knowledge of assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This phase 3 multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial was conducted at 119 sites in nine countries.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, the protocol was available, coprimary and key secondary outcomes and estimands were prespecified, and multiplicity was controlled, providing little indication of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The type I error rate was strongly controlled within each estimand independently for evaluation of coprimary and key secondary end points with a graphical approach.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged some concerns, driven by insufficient reporting of sequence generation/allocation concealment and appreciable, differential attrition requiring imputation. Blinding, objective outcome measurement, intention-to-treat analysis, prospective registration, and prespecified multiplicity-controlled reporting otherwise support low risk.
